title: qa-verify verify.json — mode=fix-verify (the loop's fix-verification verdict)
description:
The output of qa-verify in its DEFAULT mode ('fix-verify'), written to <evid_root>/<key>/verify.json. Note the two qa-verify modes point OPPOSITE ways and have separate contracts: here `pass` means the bug is GONE (the replay went RED→GREEN against the fixed build); in contracts/qa-verify.repro-judge.json `pass` means the bug IS present. Do not validate one against the other.

WHY THIS CONTRACT EXISTS. Without a schema the fix-verify artifact was the one major seam file nothing could check: run after run emitted `verdict: pass` at high confidence with masking_suspected:false, and neither the shape nor the claim was ever tested. dev-pre-pr v1.1.0 now BLOCKS on this artifact (checks.fix_verified), and the checker node reads it at the diamond's convergence point, so its shape is load-bearing for the loop's central safety property: a tier may shrink how much is verified, never whether.

BLINDNESS. This artifact must be produced by an agent that did NOT write the fix — invoked with Agent, never Skill (see dev-loop-defect/references/recipe-engine.md, 'Blind judging'). `judged_blind` records whether that held; a false value is a contract-valid artifact describing an invalid verdict, and the checker treats it as such.

verdict.description: 'pass' = the bug is GONE: the replay oracle went RED→GREEN against the fixed build AND an independent read of the app confirms it. 'fail' = the oracle ran and the bug is still there. 'partial' = the symptom changed but is not resolved. 'blocked' = NO EVIDENCE about the fix (replay-oracle.sh exit 2, app unreachable, no oracle) — this is an absent test, not a failed fix, so the router escalates rather than burning a re-fix on it. A 'pass' carrying masking_suspected:true is a fail (R3) and dev-pre-pr blocks on it.

confidence.description: How strongly the evidence supports the verdict. Capped < 80 when masking_suspected is true. The checker node enforces a per-tier floor (80 at T0/T1, 85 at T2) and flags anything below it as too low to merge into a readiness verdict.

masking_suspected.description: R3. True when the replay may have gone green because the symptom was suppressed rather than the root cause fixed — a swallowed exception, a silenced log, a narrow special-case. A true value makes a 'pass' non-shippable: dev-pre-pr blocks, and the recipe must NOT write a fix_lesson (a lesson learned from a mask poisons future recall).

key.description: The ticket key. The checker node compares this against the run's key to catch a cross-wired artifact — two runs sharing an evidence directory, or an agent handed the wrong path.

replay.description: The oracle transition in the loop's shorthand, e.g. 'red→green'. On a feature loop there is no defect to go red, so 'feature-ac:<n>/<m>' (acceptance criteria met) is used instead.

replay_note.description: How the replay was actually executed, including any degradation — e.g. that playwright-cli could not run locally and the assertions were executed in the sandbox browser instead. An honest note here is what stops a narrowed verification from reading as a full one.

observed_quote.description: What the judge independently OBSERVED, in its own words — DOM/console/network state read directly, never a success toast taken at face value.

expected_verbatim.description: The expected behaviour copied verbatim from qa-repro's oracle. Verbatim so the judge grades against the recorded expectation rather than a remembered paraphrase of it.

judge_rationale.description: Why this verdict, in one or two sentences a human can check against the evidence.

must_haves.description: The checks the verdict rests on, each with its own result — so a 'pass' can be audited item by item rather than trusted wholesale.

video2.description: Path or URL of the AFTER recording (<KEY>-fixed.gif/.mp4), the second half of the two-video evidence pair.

media.description: Capture-time evidence URLs from the evidence_store adapter, same shape as qa-repro.json v1.2.0.

judged_blind.description: Did a context that had NOT written the fix produce this verdict? True only when qa-verify was invoked via Agent with a fresh context. False means the producer graded itself — the artifact may be well-formed but the verdict is not independent, and it must not be treated as verification. Absent on pre-1.0.0 artifacts, where it is unknown rather than true.

model.description: The model this judge ran on. The checker node enforces judge-strength: a judge weaker than the producer it grades yields an invalid verdict, not merely a weaker one.

attempt.description: Which verify attempt produced this artifact, 1-based. Added because the retry audit had to be reconstructed from session transcripts — no artifact recorded its own attempt number, so a re-verify was indistinguishable from a first pass after the fact.

retry_reason.description: Why this attempt happened, when attempt > 1. A retry requires transient-failure evidence (flaky-store match, infra error, timeout, oracle exit 2); a deterministic failure escalates or re-fixes instead of retrying blind.

timing.description: When this stage ran. Costs microseconds to write and is the only way to tell whether a pipeline redesign still holds months later — without it every duration has to be reconstructed from session transcripts, which do not always exist.
